newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bond prices end up led by CPI-linked bonds.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bond prices end up led by CPI-linked bonds.

text.p: Prices for Israeli bonds, except those linked to the dollar, closed higher on Monday as bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) rose for the fourth consecutive day, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 169.13.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct at 159.96
Volume was high at 189 million shekels.
"The provident funds had positive results in October and they are less pressured to sell bonds now. The market is very stable and bonds were rising across the board," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

"Last week the long inflation-linked bonds fell because the Bank of Israel said it will issue new linked bonds. Following the announcement yields rose from 4.5 percent to 4.7 percent, which is attractive again," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
Traders said the main gainers were the seven-to-10 year CPI-linked bonds, which rose 0.27 percent.

"Unlinked bonds continue to rise. With yields of 16.4 percent and (1996) inflation expectations of around 10 percent these bonds are very interesting. The Makams (which are also unlinked) are offering yields of 15.0-15.5 percent, which is also attractive," the Hapoalim trader said.
Traders noted that dollar-linked bonds continued to decline on low volume.

Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity. Provident funds are long-term savings funds which enjoy special tax benefits.
